stem.text: The end-product of a metabolic pathway can act as a competitive inhibitor. This is called end-product inhibition and allows a cell to control a metabolic pathway.
The diagram shows a metabolic pathway where the end-product could act as an inhibitor of enzyme W.

stem.alt: Flow diagram of a pathway: substrate, intermediate 1, intermediate 2, intermediate 3 and end-product in a vertical chain linked by arrows labelled enzyme W, enzyme X, enzyme Y and enzyme Z, with a feedback arrow labelled inhibition from end-product back to substrate.

stem.text: What would be the effect if enzyme Z was inhibited by the end-product instead of enzyme W?
